messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D water tanker supplier game set in an Indian village, designed for phones and tablets.

## Requirements
- Deliver the game now without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Responsive mobile/tablet layout and usable touch controls.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Built a browser-based Three.js game titled “Jal Yatra,” with a colorful village road, tanker truck, homes, villagers, touch/keyboard driving, water deliveries, score and rupee rewards.
- Used a CDN import for Three.js; game requires an internet connection to load it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game in `index.html`, including 3D scenery, responsive HUD, controls, delivery/score loop, pause, sound toggle and win/retry screens.
- Opened the game in Playwright and inspected desktop and 390×844 mobile screenshots.
- Verified the extracted module JavaScript with `node --check`.
- Started a local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.

### Active
- Final browser verification: starting gameplay and holding ArrowUp did not dismiss the overlay in a later test, although an earlier test successfully started the route; investigate this inconsistent interaction.
- Verify and fix any gameplay issues, then capture and inspect the latest mobile/desktop JPEG screenshots.

### Blocked
- Browser console reported no game-module errors; browser verification is inconsistent as noted above.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` start/pause/overlay event flow and reproduce why the overlay remains visible after clicking Start.
2. Test driving, braking, delivery, pause/resume and the five-delivery win condition in the browser.
3. Save and inspect a final small JPEG screenshot; report the implementation and any assumptions or limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Most recent visual-check screenshot; ignored by Git.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is the primary new game file.
- Playwright ran at `http://localhost:3002`; browser renderer uses SwiftShader/software rendering in this environment.
